concerns.text: T015 logic states: 'Extract object trajectories... OR simulate... OR use optical flow...'. This contradicts the 'NEW (Revision Concern)' note in the same file which explicitly removes optical flow fallbacks. Allowing optical flow as a fallback for physics scoring violates FR-002 (CPU-based physics filter) and Constitution Principle VI (Physics-Consistency Verification) by substituting a visual heuristic for a physics simulation, effectively weakening the requirement to 'score trajectory continuity' via simulation.

T037 (MuJoCo independent validation) allows a fallback to 'distinct ground truth generated from prompts' (T037a) if real data (T037b) is missing. This violates FR-008 and Constitution Principle VI, which mandate validation against 'real-world data or a strictly independent engine on actual physical outcomes'. Generating ground truth from the same prompts used for generation creates a circular dependency (synthetic-to-synthetic validation) rather than an independent verification of physical consistency against reality or a distinct physical engine on real data.

T013 states: 'If CPU inference fails... trigger offload to Kaggle GPU'. While the plan mentions offload, the task description does not explicitly mandate that the *primary* execution path must fail loudly if offload is unavailable, risking a silent fallback to a 'fake' CPU generation or a hanging process. FR-007 and Constitution Principle I require strict adherence to the CPU-only constraint for the core pipeline; if the model cannot run on CPU, the task must abort, not silently offload without a defined failure mode for the offload itself.

T033a requires loading PhysisForcing baseline results from the paper. The task lacks a verification step to ensure these numbers are machine-readable and reproducible before use. Relying on 'paper results' without a mechanism to verify their source or format risks violating Constitution Principle IV (Single Source of Truth) if the numbers are hand-typed or unverifiable, effectively weakening the requirement for 'Verified Accuracy' in the evaluation phase.

T016 (Filtering) triggers T019b (Augmentation) if n < 30, but T019b is listed as a dependency of T016 in Phase 4. This circular dependency logic means the augmentation logic may not be available when the filtering logic attempts to call it. This violates the internal consistency of the execution plan and risks failing the acceptance criteria for FR-009 (Data Augmentation) if the pipeline cannot dynamically augment the dataset before finalizing the curated set.
